shared_edgbaston_context.review_scope: Visual review of all four pages of each original BGS PDF; factual paraphrases for a preliminary desk study, without design parameters.

shared_pages.description: Same historical site-location plans in both PDFs, with different BGS wrappers. Drawing 1, contract 1829, September 1988.

Same exploratory-hole location plan in both PDFs. Drawing 2, September 1988; shows BH1, BH2, BH3 and TP1 to TP6, a historical proposed-building footprint, an approximately 1 m retaining wall and vegetation. This is a historical plan, not a current site boundary.

Same west-to-east geological section in both PDFs. Drawing 3, September 1988; depicts BH1 to BH3 and trial pits with questioned correlations. It explicitly states that ground levels were extrapolated from another drawing. The interpreted boulder-clay key does not turn the individual logs' sandy-clay descriptions into a confirmed site-wide till unit. Do not infer current groundwater or a surveyed borehole datum from this section.

report_family_gap.note: The shared exploratory plan and section show BH3 and TP1 to TP6 in addition to the two individual logs reviewed here. Obtain the complete investigation report and remaining original logs before finalising the ground model or GI scope; no detailed findings for those additional holes have been transcribed from these diagrams.

conditional_gi_implications.inference: Reconcile the drilling-date discrepancy and georeference the historical plan to the actual development before transferring any depths or observations.

If relevant to the actual site and works, target made-ground thickness, shallow soft pockets, clay/granular variability and the sand-to-weak-sandstone transition. The two historical fill bases are 1.10 and 0.60 m, and sandstone tops 6.50 and 5.50 m; these are observations at those holes only.
Select investigation equipment for cobbles and weak rock; consider coring where rock quality affects design. Chiselling and short penetration seating blows do not establish competent bearing rock.
Obtain appropriately screened and surveyed groundwater monitoring with repeat observations where relevant to the works. Historic dry drilling notes do not justify omitting groundwater assessment.

review_limits: No current site ground profile, design parameter, foundation recommendation or hazard absence has been established.
Six reviewed records are not an exhaustive search of the 423 reported index matches in the enclosing box.
